summary: The stored positive rating rests on an essential amino acid mixture and a whey drink, neither of which is leucine alone, and on muscle protein synthesis over hours. A 2022 meta-analysis of 17 RCTs (35845777) found that leucine alone did not improve muscle mass or strength in older people; benefit came with combinations including vitamin D. Trials of free leucine with training (32079916, 40926079, 31577520) added nothing. Two small trials were positive (32230954, 37923932), and two reviews read leucine more favorably (32483625, 40805998), the second calling its evidence low quality and limited when leucine is used alone. Evidence conflicts, with no clear benefit for the labels' free leucine.
